Git and GitHub are related, but they are not the same thing.

```text
Git     = version-control system
GitHub  = hosting + collaboration + review + automation around repositories
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Key ideas
`remote` `clone` `fork` `issue` `pull request` `review`
`Actions` `README` `release` `Pages`
:::

## Collaboration loop

```text
Issue
 ↓
Branch
 ↓
Commits
 ↓
Push
 ↓
Pull Request
 ↓
Review
 ↓
Merge
```

## Learn interactively

**GitHub Skills:**  
https://skills.github.com/

**GitHub Get Started:**  
https://docs.github.com/en/get-started

**GitHub Actions:**  
https://docs.github.com/en/actions

**GitHub Pages:**  
https://docs.github.com/en/pages

## A Data Science repository should explain itself

```text
project/
├── README.md
├── data/          # or instructions to obtain data
├── notebooks/
├── src/
├── tests/
├── requirements.txt
└── results/
```

A strong README answers:

1. What problem does this solve?
2. What data is used?
3. How do I run it?
4. What did you find/build?
5. How is the repository organized?

::: {.callout-tip}
## Portfolio principle
Three understandable, reproducible projects usually communicate more than dozens of unexplained notebooks.
:::
